title: Closure of d-DNNF under negation
formal: Do a constant \(c>0\) and an integer \(k\ge 1\) exist such that, for every finite variable set X and every d-DNNF circuit C over X of size s, there is a d-DNNF circuit D over X of size at most \(c(s+1)^{k}\) computing the Boolean complement of C on every assignment \(X->\{0,1\}\)? No algorithm for finding D within that bound is required.
definitions: An NNF circuit is a finite rooted directed acyclic graph whose leaves are constants 0,1 or literals x,not-x for x in X, and whose internal nodes are AND or OR gates. Edges run from a gate to its inputs. The variable set of a subcircuit comprises the variables occurring in its reachable literals. Decomposable means that the input subcircuits of every AND gate have pairwise disjoint variable sets. Deterministic means that no assignment to X makes two different inputs of any OR gate both true. A d-DNNF satisfies both properties. Size is the total number of vertices plus edges; fan-in is arbitrary and part of that size. Evaluation has the usual Boolean meaning. No negation gates above leaves, additional variables, or requirement of compatibility with a common variable decomposition tree is allowed. Constants c,k are independent of X and C. The output D may use any decompositions meeting these conditions.
answer_criterion: Prove the universal polynomial size bound, or prove that no constants c,k satisfy it. Algorithmic difficulty of producing a small complement alone does not refute this size-existence statement.
why: Deterministic decomposable circuits represent Boolean solution sets while supporting exact counting. Closure under complement asks whether a compact representation of satisfying assignments necessarily gives a comparably compact representation of nonsatisfying assignments, independently of construction time.

importance.reason: A central representational-closure question in knowledge compilation that separates succinctness from the cost of performing a logical operation.

context_blocks.text: Decomposability prevents conjunctions from sharing variables and determinism prevents disjunctions from sharing satisfying assignments. Negating a circuit syntactically need not preserve both properties.

Structured d-DNNFs additionally respect a variable decomposition tree. The 2024 negative result for that restricted class cannot be transferred automatically to unrestricted d-DNNF, since a complementary circuit here may use other decompositions.

The STACS 2026 discussion retains complementation as an open question. The separate algorithmic question asks for a polynomial-time procedure producing the complement. Such a procedure implies the size bound on this card; the converse is not established. Both targets are retained because an existence theorem would settle a representation barrier without necessarily supplying the algorithmic transformation.
The stronger polynomial-time construction question is retained as TCS-0306. The existence of small complementary circuits does not by itself give an efficient algorithm for constructing them.

progress.text: Vinall-Smeeth proves that structured d-DNNF is not closed under polynomial-size negation.
Amarilli and coauthors identify unstructured d-DNNF complementation as an open issue in their STACS paper.
Amarilli's maintained question list explicitly distinguishes the unresolved polynomial-size question from polynomial-time construction.
